title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 117 (Resolutions and agreements to be filed)

content.overview: Section 117 requires filing with the Registrar, within thirty days, copies of resolutions and agreements covered by subsection (3), with any section 102 explanatory statement. Failure to file attracts a company penalty of ₹10,000 plus ₹100 per day of continuing failure, capped at ₹2,00,000, and a separate officer-in-default penalty of ₹10,000 plus ₹100 per day, capped at ₹50,000.

content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 117 (Resolutions and agreements to be filed). A copy of each resolution or agreement covered by subsection (3), together with any section 102 explanatory statement annexed to the meeting notice, must be filed with the Registrar within thirty days of passing or making it, in the prescribed manner and with the prescribed fees. The covered categories include special resolutions; certain unanimous resolutions that would otherwise require a special resolution; specified Board resolutions or agreements concerning appointment, re-appointment, renewal or variation of a managing director's terms; specified class resolutions/agreements; resolutions under section 180(1)(a) and (c); voluntary winding-up resolutions under section 304; and resolutions under section 179(3), subject to the statutory provisos. If the company fails to file within the period in subsection (1), it is liable to a penalty of ₹10,000 and, for continuing failure, a further ₹100 per day after the first, capped at ₹2,00,000. Every officer in default, including a liquidator if any, is liable to ₹10,000 and, for continuing failure, a further ₹100 per day after the first, capped at ₹50,000. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Filing duty and deadline
sections.body: A copy of every resolution or agreement covered by subsection (3), together with any section 102 explanatory statement annexed to the meeting notice, must be filed with the Registrar within thirty days of passing or making it, in the prescribed manner and with prescribed fees. A resolution altering the articles and covered agreements must also be embodied in or annexed to copies of the articles issued after the resolution or agreement.

sections.heading: Covered resolutions and agreements
sections.body: Subsection (3) includes special resolutions; certain unanimous resolutions that would otherwise require a special resolution; specified Board resolutions or agreements relating to appointment, re-appointment, renewal or variation of a managing director's terms; specified class resolutions/agreements; resolutions under section 180(1)(a) and (c); voluntary winding-up resolutions under section 304; and resolutions passed under section 179(3), subject to the statutory provisos.

sections.heading: Penalty for non-filing
sections.body: If the company fails to file within the period specified in subsection (1), the company is liable to a penalty of ₹10,000 and, for continuing failure, a further ₹100 per day after the first, subject to a maximum of ₹2,00,000. Every officer in default, including a liquidator if any, is liable to ₹10,000 and, for continuing failure, a further ₹100 per day after the first, subject to a maximum of ₹50,000.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming every ordinary resolution must be filed under section 117.
misconceptions.correction: Identify whether the resolution/agreement falls within subsection (3) and any applicable proviso.

misconceptions.trap: Using the older fine/imprisonment penalty language instead of the substituted subsection (2).
misconceptions.correction: Use the current penalty structure: ₹10,000 plus ₹100 per day, capped at ₹2,00,000 for the company and ₹50,000 for every officer in default.

misconceptions.trap: Ignoring the thirty-day filing deadline or the section 102 explanatory statement where applicable.
misconceptions.correction: Check the deadline, prescribed manner/fees and any section 102 explanatory statement.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What resolutions must be filed under section 117?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Those specified in subsection (3), including special resolutions and other listed matters, together with any section 102 statement, within thirty days. Verify the current form and exemptions.

examTips: Do not state that every ordinary resolution must be filed.
Mention the thirty-day period and the need to check exemptions and current forms.
revisionPoints: File covered resolutions/agreements within thirty days.
Check subsection (3) categories and provisos; not every ordinary resolution is covered.
Officer in default: ₹10,000 plus ₹100/day, capped at ₹50,000.
